# Midjourney V8.1: What's New and How to Try It Today

Picture this: you're scrolling through Instagram, spot a gorgeous illustrated poster, and wish you could make something half that lovely for your small business, your kid's birthday invite, or just for fun. That feeling — "I wish I could make that" — is exactly the gap AI image tools are closing, and the latest Midjourney update makes that gap a little smaller.

## What just happened with Midjourney

Midjourney (an AI tool that turns your written descriptions into images) has rolled out a new version called **V8.1**. It's now available in two places: inside the **Discord** chat app, and directly on **midjourney.com** through their own website. The big story is image quality — V8.1 produces sharper, cleaner pictures than the previous version. You'll notice this most in two features experienced Midjourney users love: **SREFs** and **Moodboards**.

## What's an SREF, and what's a Moodboard?

Two new-ish terms worth knowing:

- A **SREF** (short for *Style Reference*) is a piece of artwork or photo you upload so Midjourney can match its visual style — think colours, textures, mood — without copying the actual content.
- A **Moodboard** is similar but more flexible: you feed it several images at once, and Midjourney blends the overall "feel" of all of them into your new image.

Think of it like this: a SREF is asking a painter "match the style of *this one* painting", while a Moodboard is saying "match the *vibe* of these five paintings together." V8.1 pays closer attention to these references now, so your results look more like what you had in mind.

## How to actually try V8.1 — step by step

Here's the path from zero to your first image:

1. **Pick your doorway.** Head to **midjourney.com** in your browser for the simplest start, or use **Discord** if you already have an account. Both run V8.1.
2. **Sign in or set up an account.** You'll need a Midjourney subscription to generate images. There *may* be a free trial for new accounts, but availability changes by region and promotion — so don't count on it. If you don't see a free option on the sign-up screen, you'll go straight to the paid plans.
3. **Find the prompt box.** On **midjourney.com**, the prompt box sits in the **centre of the screen**, labelled *"Imagine"* — type your description there. On **Discord**, open one of the **#general** or **#newbies** channels in the Midjourney server, and type your prompt **directly into the chat bar at the bottom** of the window. If your Discord looks different, look for any text field that says *"Message #channel-name"* — that's the one.
4. **Add a SREF or Moodboard (optional).** On **midjourney.com**, click the **"+" icon** on the left side of the prompt box to upload an image file from your computer. On **Discord**, simply **drag and drop** the image into the chat a few seconds before you send your prompt, then type `--sref` followed by the image link. If you can't find the upload button, try the **paperclip icon** in the chat bar — that's the standard attachment shortcut.
5. **Write your prompt.** Try something simple like *"a cosy café at dusk, warm lighting, illustrated style"*. Then press **Enter** (or click **Generate** on the website).
6. **Refine.** Don't love the first result? Click **Vary** or **Vary (Subtle)** on the website, or type `/imagine` again on Discord with small tweaks. Most great images take a few tries.

> **If your screen looks different from what we describe**, don't panic — Midjourney updates its interface regularly. Look for the words **"Imagine," "Generate,"** or **"Upload"** anywhere on the page; those buttons always do what you'd expect.

## What this means for you

- **If you create for fun**: V8.1 is a lovely excuse to experiment. Try generating a birthday card, a phone wallpaper, or a fantasy book cover. The sharper output means your images look more "finished" out of the gate.
- **If you run a small business or side project**: Better style-matching means your social posts, blog headers, and product mockups can share a consistent look — even when you generate them on different days. That visual consistency usually takes hours of design work; V8.1 gets you closer with a few prompts.
- **If you're brand new to AI images**: Start on **midjourney.com** rather than Discord — the website is calmer and easier to learn. Once you've made a few images you like, you'll naturally get more confident with prompts.

## Wrap-up

Midjourney V8.1 isn't a reinvention — it's a polish. Sharper images, better attention to your style references, and easier access through both Discord and the website. If you've been curious about AI image generation, this is a friendly moment to try it.

**Your next step today:** hop onto **midjourney.com**, create an account, and generate one image of something you'd genuinely enjoy — a pet portrait, a dream kitchen, a poster for your favourite hobby. See what V8.1 can do with your idea.
